key_insight: Compact multimodal language models can answer structured pulmonary embolism questions better when they combine CTPA with EHR evidence, with the strongest gains seen in Gemma4 E4B and E2B.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests efficient AI systems may help earlier PE risk detection and support prognostic assessment in settings where imaging and longitudinal records are both available.
method: Built an INSPECT-based benchmark for pulmonary embolism using 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients.
Formulated 8 diagnostic and prognostic tasks as structured clinical question answering problems.
Compared efficient MLLMs across CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR inputs using zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluation showed better performance when EHR evidence was added, especially for CTPA+EHR inputs, while PE diagnosis outperformed prognostic tasks such as readmission prediction.
watch_item: Performance is still task-dependent and weaker for prognosis, so real-world use would need careful validation before any clinical deployment.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
